results.term_definition: Gravity is the mutual attraction of objects with mass. In classical mechanics, any object with a mass always exerts a force of attraction on another object with a mass. This attractive force is what we know as gravity. Einstein's theory of general relativity recasts gravity as a curvature of spacetime rather than a force. However the classical approximation of gravity is still accurate in most scenarios. The more massive an object is, the stronger its gravitational force/distortion of spacetime and hence the stronger the pull on other objects.
